reference: The runnable contract expectations are based on Bash type/help builtin behavior and the documented ip synopsis and capability text in the loadable documentation. Operational parity is not run here: a future isolated Linux VM or controlled rtnetlink mock should compare against iproute2 ip with explicitly seeded network state.
coverage: Bash recognizes ip as a builtin and exposes its short help metadata.
The full help metadata retains the documented rtnetlink scope, CAP_NET_ADMIN requirement, and unique-prefix contract.
Deferred read-only link, address, route, rule, and neighbour query output and filters.
Deferred link and address state changes in a disposable network namespace.
Deferred route, policy-rule, and neighbour updates against seeded state.
Deferred batch parsing, error handling, and -force continuation with a controlled rtnetlink endpoint.
exclusions: No ip operation was invoked: even read-only operations would access kernel network state, and mutations require privileged state changes.
There are no parity cases because operation fixtures need controlled rtnetlink state; their outputs cannot be honestly inferred from this candidate or from this host.
The suite does not exercise real interfaces, packet exchange, network peers, or CAP_NET_ADMIN behavior.

cases.purpose: Check the Bash type builtin identifies the shipped ip command as a builtin and that Bash can retrieve its short synopsis metadata.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t ip) == builtin ]]
synopsis=$(help -s ip)
[[ $synopsis == ip:* ]]
printf 'ip builtin and short help available\n'
cases.stdout: ip builtin and short help available

cases.purpose: Check the full Bash help entry exposes documented implementation scope, privilege requirements, and keyword-prefix behavior without invoking ip operations.
cases.script:
details=$(help ip)
[[ $details == *rtnetlink* ]]
[[ $details == *CAP_NET_ADMIN* ]]
[[ $details == *'Unique prefixes are accepted for implemented objects, verbs, and selectors.'* ]]
printf 'documented ip help contract present\n'

cases.purpose: Compare link, address, route, rule, and neighbour show output, including JSON/brief forms, family filtering, and selectors against independent rtnetlink state.
cases.reason: No seeded namespace exists; read-only queries of a script-owned namespace are safe in the VM.

cases.purpose: Exercise link up/down, MTU and address setters, dummy/veth creation, and deletion while checking resulting link state.
Exercise address add, delete, change, replace, flush, and address selectors against a known interface state.
cases.reason: No fixture runs ip; the VM can provide a private namespace with a seeded dummy interface, so this is fixture work.

cases.purpose: Exercise route add/delete/replace/flush, policy-rule add/delete/flush, and neighbour add/change/replace/delete with deterministic state checks.
Check batch-file tokenization, blank lines, stopping at the first failing command, and -force continuation using a bounded sequence with observable state.
cases.reason: Needs observable rtnetlink state in a private namespace; no fixture exists.
